title: Per-stage token cost decomposition and auto-mute alerting
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds per-stage (system/user/instruction) token-cost breakdowns, a new dashboard with cohort panels, and an adaptive alert muting rule for noisy tenants. Backwards compatible; no API changes.
description:
Motivation: We have good per-invocation token cost telemetry but it's coarse — teams frequently need to know which part of a prompt/response (system prompt, user prompt, instruction blocks, model-generated continuation) drives token cost and latency regressions. This PR introduces a token-cost decomposition pipeline and end-to-end UX: 1) runtime emits per-segment token counters and cumulative latency tags; 2) trace enrichment synthesizes 'stage' spans (system/user/instruction/generation) for each invocation; 3) metrics rollup produces per-tenant and per-model per-stage cost histograms and a compact cohort index used by alerting. In addition, we observed alert fatigue from tenants with noisy dev traffic. This PR adds an auto-mute policy for alerts where >80% of noise is from a small set of callers for a short window, and a manual-unmute flow in the Console.

What changed (high level): - Runtime span enrichment: small change to request wrapper that emits stage boundaries and token deltas (instrumentation guarded behind a feature flag). - Trace-sidecar enrichment job: lightweight sampler that merges prefix metadata (client-side stage markers) into spans and tags high-cost prefixes for retention. - Metrics rollups: new per-stage token_cost_* metrics (sum, p50/p95/p99 histograms) and per-stage latency histograms. - Alerting: new SLO attenuation rule and an auto-mute controller that can suppress noisy alerts with audit trail and suggested escalation. - Dashboards: new Observability > Cost > Per-stage Cost Breakdown dashboard with cohort selectors (model, tenant, route, prompt-stage) and a compact waterfall panel for per-invocation stage latency. - Tests and migration: migration adds compact histogram series and a lightweight index for prefix fingerprints; migration is backwards-compatible and small storage delta.

Review notes and tradeoffs: - Accuracy vs overhead: per-stage counters are emitted as deltas; we kept per-token instrumentation coarse-grained (per-chunk) to avoid per-token RPC overhead. Sampling is keyed to cost density so we keep retention budget focused on expensive prefixes. - Storage: histograms add modest cardinality. We aggregate into fixed cardinality cohort keys (tenant, model, stage, route hash) to avoid explosion. - Rollout plan: feature flag default off for hosted customers. Enable in a canary cluster, run nightly cohort reports to validate distribution, then flip on for more tenants. - Security/PII: stage markers are metadata only; we do not ship prompt text to metrics or index unless tenant opt-in; trace retention for payloads follows existing PII rules.

Review conversation (summary): Arjun: "Nice incremental approach — can we tighten the sampling threshold defaults?" — reply: "Lowered defaults in config and added per-tenant override. Included tests." Lucie: "Dashboard looks great; can we add a quick link from invocation detail to the waterfall?" — reply: "Added Console link generation and tests." Ben: "Auto-mute auditor needs to surface rationale to SRE playbooks." — reply: "Audit events now include rule fingerprint and top-3 callers; added to event schema." QA: "E2E flakes in the first run due to query timeout; reran and green." Merge decision: squash-and-merge after green CI and final doc stub added. Deployed to canary on 2025-12-01; monitored for 48h; no regression in P95 latency or token-cost budgets.

notes_for_ops: Feature flag: observability.per_stage_cost = off by default for all hosted clusters. Canary enablement steps included in deploy/README. Migration: run 001_add_stage_histograms.sql during a low-traffic window; rollup job can backfill limited window (configurable). Auto-mute policy defaults: window=10m, noise_threshold=80%, mute_ttl=30m. Manual unmute via Console with audit log entry required.
